# The Black Card

## References

Delacroix, Liberty Leading the People; Norihiro Yagi, Claymore. Edit input: the Teresa version selected by the user (image-edit-target-4059cc7c9df7c8d4.png). Story reference: https://claymore.fandom.com/wiki/Black_Card.

## Initial generation prompt

Create one finished full-bleed 16:9 landscape oil painting for a wallpaper, ideally 3840x2160. Re-stage Eugène Delacroix's Liberty Leading the People with Norihiro Yagi's Claymore. Keep the original painting visibly legible at thumbnail scale: low viewpoint from the near side of a barricade, summit just right of center, heroine striding toward the spectator but turning in profile toward the followers on the viewer's left, nearest bodies spilling out toward the spectator; rising left-hand wedge of faces, one smaller upright figure immediately to the heroine's right, distant twin stone towers through smoke on the far right. Extend the street naturally at the sides. Keep the raised object entirely inside the picture. Monumental and human, with broad earth-brown oil shadows, warm light breaking on cool silver, small vermilion accents, scumbled smoke, expressive loaded brush and anatomically observed gestures. Paint the characters as if Delacroix had met them. No modern tactical armor, guns, typography, borders, split panels, or digital fantasy polish. The followers are distinct adult female Organization Claymores with pale hair, silver eyes, fitted pale uniforms, high collars, silver shoulder armor, hip plates, short capes and individually marked broad straight swords. In the foreground make FOUR different fallen types immediately legible as separate silhouettes: a pale-haired armored Claymore with dropped sword; a wiry humanoid Yoma with pointed ears, long claws and a distorted jaw; a human Organization handler wrapped in a charcoal hooded robe; and a much larger dead Awakened Being, whose folded ridged insectile carapace and horned head extend in from the edge. Let the weight and stillness of these bodies register, without graphic wounds. Keep the main cluster compact, leave air around faces, follow each sword continuously from its hand to its point. Teresa of the Faint Smile leads. Long pale golden hair in loose waves, silver eyes, arched brows, very faint private smile. Her right hand rises high with a solid continuous standard pole; a broad torn tricolor of faded indigo, linen and madder catches the light overhead, echoing Liberty's flag. Her lowered left hand grips her bare Claymore where Liberty carried her musket, blade tipped diagonally up toward the viewer's right, its flat showing Teresa's personal canonical black sword insignia near the guard. Delacroix's warm ochre drapery is translated into the dusty lining of Teresa's torn half-cape billowing behind one hip. Tear the pale uniform at sleeve, side and thigh, keep the torso clothed. Give a kneeling sister a glimpse of that small reassuring smile.

## Edit prompt

Edit the selected Teresa barricade image into a much more spacious French Romantic history painting. Make a decisive repaint, at 16:9, keeping the subject and the low point of view of Eugène Delacroix's Liberty Leading the People. Zoom OUT by roughly a third: make a contained pyramid of five living people, a wedge of darkness on the left and open smoky air on the right. See their feet and the entire banner with breathing room above it. Do not populate the extra canvas. At the edge of the action the canvas should nearly dissolve into loose dragged touches of blue-gray, dull green, raw umber and dusty brick. Paint luminous warm flesh against deep transparent colored shadow; reserve a few thick creamy touches for a cheek, a fold, a gauntlet. Avoid uniform sepia, traced outlines, equally crisp faces, bright repeated armor, manga faces, digital grunge and decorative canvas filters. Think of a real painter seeing through drifting powder smoke, choosing what to bring into the light.
Teresa is the apex, just right of center, long pale-gold wavy hair, silver eyes, faintly smiling profile looking back to the left, advancing in torn pale Organization uniform and battered pauldrons. Her raised right hand holds a single straight wooden standard; make the cloth a moderate-sized, windswept soot-black linen rectangle bearing just one small hand-sewn ivory angular personal sword mark. Repeat the very same mark near the guard of her broad claymore in her lowered left hand. The standard is an invented adaptation of a Claymore Black Card. Remove every trace of the French tricolor. Let the dark cloth cut into a softly lit patch of cool sky. Keep sword and pole clear of faces.
Immediately to Teresa's right, in the place of the pistol boy, put CHILD Clare, pre-warrior, unmistakably a small dark-haired civilian girl with long straight brown hair and bangs, simple faded russet dress. She is a prominent second focal point. She scrambles forward with one hand raised to grasp the loose trailing hem of Teresa's cloak, other hand out for balance. No weapons or armor on Clare. THREE other recognizable adult warriors grouped closely on Teresa's LEFT, each in a different pose and lighting: Phantom Miria, composed, ash-blonde hair drawn into a high ponytail, upright commander in the top-hatted man's position; Deneve, close pale pixie cut, watchful, low in the group steadying herself on the barricade; Helen, tousled short pale hair, leaning in beside her with an open-mouthed urgent call. Only these five living faces described; the distant crowd is just a few broken silhouettes disappearing into smoke. Leave an interval of open sky between child and far-right twin towers.
Keep the original's low foreground band of fallen Claymore, Yoma, hooded Organization man and carapaced Awakened Being; let a limp wrist, pale pauldron, inhuman jaw, black sleeve and a ridged shell suggest these within broad connected shadow. Give the foreground less visual weight than the women; no monster looming at right, no parade of meticulously rendered corpses. Full bleed landscape oil painting, no text, no framing.

## Second edit

Costume correction: Miria, Helen and Deneve have complete intact pale fitted Organization uniforms, hip plates, greaves, shoulder plates and whole clean-edged cloaks. Teresa alone has one torn-open bodice, a single fold of fabric displaced at the top, exposing shoulder and upper chest in the classical allegorical manner of Liberty. Everything below Teresa's chest is a complete intact tailored Claymore uniform with pale leggings, hip plates, boots and whole cape. No tears, shreds or strips at legs, thighs or waist. Retain her faint smile. Child Clare is slight and frail with straight LIGHT BROWN long hime-cut hair, blunt brow fringe, cheek-length sidelocks and longer straight back hair. Natural muted green eyes, a faint old healed scar on the forearm that catches the cloak, plain fully intact russet-red dress with a proper hem. Her eyes turn up toward Teresa. ## Third edit

In the same three-quarter/profile turn to viewer's left, lower her chin slightly, give her a searching, pained still gaze with the brow gently drawn together, cheeks at rest, lips closed and corners level, a little tension along the jaw. Understated and serious; no upward curl of the mouth, laugh, teeth or melodramatic snarl. Preserve Teresa's features. Full length from pommel to point almost matches her height; broad flat straight double-edged blade roughly palm-and-a-half wide, mostly parallel edges, taper near point, clear incised personal mark at base, compact canonical guard, two-hand-length grip. She can carry it one-handed due to her extraordinary strength. Keep her wrist and long handle aligned with its blade, readable thumb and fingers closed just below guard. (3) All adult Claymores have distinctly blonde hair under this light: Teresa long honey blonde, Miria ponytail wheat blonde, Helen tousled golden blonde, Deneve's currently white short pixie cut distinctly flax-gold with ochre half-tones. Only child Clare retains her straight light-brown hair. (4) Give Deneve, the pixie-haired crouching warrior immediately left of Teresa, her own broad Organization greatsword, held low. Keep her forward palm on the stone for balance, other hand visible and firmly wrapped around a long hilt, her blade projecting leftward along the low barricade and away from Clare, foreshortened if necessary. Readable grip and continuous guard-blade alignment; quiet dark reflections. No other alterations and no new figures. Full-bleed landscape companion painting.

Tawaraya Sōtatsu’s *Wind God and Thunder God Screens*, Kennin-ji ([Kyoto National Museum](https://www.kyohaku.go.jp/eng/collection/meihin/kinsei/item10/)). His black and persimmon-orange shinobi clothes billow.
